rationale: Editor restored ⲡⲣⲁⲩϣ in line 17 with question mark. Likely Lyc reflex of Sahidic ⲣⲟⲟⲩϣ 'care, anxiety, preoccupation' (Crum). The first of the four worldly concerns — 'the care of the mouth' = preoccupation with food.
Obscure verbal form on root ⲃⲉⲗ-, possibly = ⲡⲱⲗ 'be loosed/joined' or ⲡⲱⲣⲡ 'mingle.' Used in line 21 of women joining sexually with one another. Sense from context; etymology unclear.
Plural noun in war-vice catalogue alongside ⲡⲡⲟⲗⲉⲙⲟⲥ 'war' and ⲫⲓⲗⲟⲛⲓⲕⲓⲁ 'contention.' Likely Lyc plural of ⲗⲓⲃⲉ 'madness, frenzy' (Sahidic ⲗⲓⲃⲉ 'be mad'). Captures the affective-violent register.
Greek loanword ἀδικίαι 'injustices.' Lyc orthographic reduction ⲁⲇⲓ → ⲁⲓ. Standard moral vocabulary; one of the war-deeds men do to one another.

proposed_english: the four great matters / four great works
rationale: Compound: ⲡⲩⲧⲁⲩ 'the four' (Lyc, in glossary) + ⲛⲁⲃ 'great' + ⲛϩⲱⲃ 'matters/works.' Chapter-organizing term for the four worldly preoccupations (food, sex, wealth, war) for which men kill one another. Standard Manichaean ascetical-paraenetic enumeration.
Verb in line 30 ⲉⲩⲁⲭⲡⲧⲁⲩ 'that they may take them.' Likely Lyc form of ϣⲱⲡ 'receive' (with ⲭ for ϣ) or ϫⲡⲟ 'acquire' (Lyc ⲭ for ϫ). Used here of taking possession of the four worldly works.

Form in line 10 ⲡⲉⲩϩⲧⲏⲩ following 'shall place their...' before infinitive 'to speak.' Possibly Lyc plural of ϩⲏⲧ 'heart' or a noun for speech-organ (lips/tongue). Etymology uncertain; awaits parallels.
